title: 142 Administering the maternal bovine appeasing substance improves finishing performance and overall productivity of feedlot cattle
content:
Abstract
The objective of this experiment was to evaluate physiological and performance responses of feedlot steers administered the maternal bovine appeasing substance (mBAS) during a 178-d finishing period. This experiment used cattle previously assigned to a 60-d feedlot receiving study, in which 120 Angus-influenced high-risk steers received 10 mL of mBAS (Ferappease®; FERA Diagnostics and Biologicals; College Station, TX; n = 60) or 10 ml of mineral oil (CON; placebo; n = 60) at initial processing (d 0) and 14 d later. During this previous 60-d receiving period (d 0 to 61), steers were arranged in 10 drylot pens (20 × 10 m) with 5 pens/treatment and 12 steers/pen. Data collection for the current experiment began on d 61 relative to initial processing, using the steers that completed the receiving period (no mortality or removal) with the same arrangements of steers/pen and pen/treatment. Briefly, 53 CON and 58 mBAS steers (5 pens/treatment; 10 to 12 steers/pen) were assigned to the growing period (d 61 to 124) when treatments were not administered. On d 124 relative to initial processing, all steers were road-transported for 16 h and returned to the same research facility for the finishing period (d 125 to 303). Steers assigned to mBAS in the receiving period were administered mBAS (10 mL) or CON upon arrival on d 125, and when administered a growth implant (d 213). Treatments were applied topically to the nuchal skin area (5 mL) and above the muzzle (5 mL). Steer body weight (BW) was recorded after a 16-h feed and water restriction on d 61, and immediately upon arrival on d 125. Steer BW on d 302 and 303 were averaged, discounted a 4% shrink, and considered final BW. Hair samples from the tail-switch were collected on d 125 and d 140. All steers were slaughtered on d 304. During the growing period, no treatment differences were observed (P ≥ 0.23) for performance parameters including average daily gain (ADG) and feed intake. No treatment effect was noted (P = 0.86) for hair cortisol concentrations. During the finishing period, ADG and gain to feed ratio were greater (P ≤ 0.04) in mBAS compared with CON, whereas feed intake and final BW did not differ (P ≥ 0.57) between treatments. No treatment effects were detected for carcass traits (P ≥ 0.24) including hot carcass weight. Collectively, mBAS administration to feedlot steers at the beginning of a 178-d finishing period and at the time of reimplanting increased growth performance without affecting feed intake.
